title: Dynamic Worker Supervision (simple_one_for_one & supervisor:start_child)
solutionExplanation: Implements a clean simple_one_for_one supervisor with a single template child spec referencing companion module session_worker, dynamic start_child appending, and active count introspection.

otpDocCards.signature: supervisor:start_child(SupRef, ChildSpec | [Arg]) -> {ok, Child} | {ok, Child, Info} | {error, Reason}
otpDocCards.description: For simple_one_for_one supervisors, appends the arguments list to the template start MFA and spawns a dynamic worker.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Synchronous child spawn and link. Returns when child init/1 completes.

otpDocCards.signature: supervisor:count_children(SupRef) -> #{specs := integer(), active := integer(), supervisors := integer(), workers := integer()}
otpDocCards.description: Returns telemetry counts of child specifications, active processes, and worker vs supervisor nodes.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(N) iteration over internal supervisor child tracking list.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does simple_one_for_one allow only ONE child specification template inside init/1?

options.label: Because simple_one_for_one is designed as a factory for an arbitrary number of identical dynamic workers spawned on demand.
options.explanation: simple_one_for_one treats its single child specification as a blueprint template. All dynamic children share the same module, restart policy, and shutdown timeout.

options.label: Because the BEAM VM memory limit prevents supervisors from holding more than one map.
options.explanation: Supervisors can hold many specs in other strategies; simple_one_for_one is conceptually a homogeneous worker factory.

options.label: Because simple_one_for_one can only ever run one process at a time.
options.explanation: It can run millions of simultaneous dynamic workers, all spawned from the single template.

options.label: Because dynamic workers are forbidden from using gen_server.
options.explanation: Dynamic workers almost always implement gen_server or gen_statem.
